newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM vows not to give in to "terrorism".
newsitem.headline: Japan PM vows not to give in to "terrorism".

text.p: Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto sought on Monday to dispel doubts about Japan's determination not to give in to rebels in the Lima hostage crisis, pledging always to fight "terrorism".

In a policy speech on the opening day of the 1997 parliamentary session, Hashimoto gave full backing to Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori for his handling of the 35-day-old siege at the Japanese ambassador's residence.

"Japan will never give in to terrorism," Hashimoto declared. "Terrorist activity is a grave challenge to all states and societies and it is vital for the international community to tackle terrorism in unity."
Marxist rebels stormed the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima on December 17, taking more than 500 hostages and demanding the release of some 400 imprisoned comrades.
Although the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels have released most hostages, they still hold 73 captives and negotiations for their freedom have stalled.
"It is extremely regrettable that the hostage crisis at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Peru remains unresolved," Hashimoto said.
But the prime minister declared his "complete confidence" in Fujimori's hardline negotiating tactics in refusing to consider the rebels' main demand for the release of their comrades.
